topic_and_scope: Assessment and validation of a newborn screening (NBS) program for multiple inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) in a tertiary care hospital in South India, with emphasis on region-specific cutoffs, follow-up dynamics, and potential for scalable implementation in India.
main_themes: Feasibility of implementing a multi-disorder NBS panel in a regional Indian setting with population-tailored cutoffs
Follow-up, adherence, and awareness gaps impacting the effectiveness of NBS and subsequent care
Policy, implementation science, and capacity-building required for national-scale NBS integration
main_findings: Manufacturer-provided cutoffs for all seven parameters were largely consistent with study-derived cutoffs in the Indian context, supporting validity of the chosen thresholds for this population.

Overall recall rate across markers was 5.55%, but only 26.7% of screen-positive infants returned for confirmatory testing, highlighting a major gap in follow-up and parental awareness, which constrained true-positive ascertainment.

key_gaps.description: Low follow-up compliance among screen-positive newborns (only 26.7% returned for retesting), hindering accurate determination of true positives and program effectiveness.
Absence of a nationwide NBS policy in India and limited population-based prevalence data for treatable IEMs, constraining scalable implementation and resource planning.

future_directions.title: Develop and validate GA- and birth-weight–adjusted cutoffs for all NBS markers across multiple Indian centers
future_directions.rationale: The study indicates that 17-OHP and other markers are influenced by gestational age and birth weight, contributing to false positives, especially in preterm or LBW infants. A multicenter effort should collect stratified data (by GA, birth weight, and sampling age) to derive percentile-based cutoffs. Prospective validation with confirmatory testing and longitudinal follow-up will confirm improved specificity and reduce unnecessary recalls. Implement standardized algorithms in routine screening workflows across tertiary and district hospitals.

future_directions.title: Strengthen follow-up infrastructure and parental engagement to improve retesting rates
future_directions.rationale: With only 26.7% of screen-positive infants returning for retesting, there is a critical need for systematic follow-up protocols. Implement automated reminder systems (calls/SMS), community health worker outreach, and transportation support. Develop a tracking dashboard to monitor who remains Lost to Follow-Up and to trigger targeted interventions. Evaluate impact on retest completion, time to diagnosis, and treatment initiation.

future_directions.title: Launch targeted community education campaigns about IEMs and NBS in rural and urban settings
future_directions.rationale: Public awareness was identified as a key barrier to follow-up. Design vernacular, culturally appropriate educational materials, including brochures, short videos, and patient stories distributed via community events, primary care clinics, and media. Assess changes in knowledge, attitudes, and screening uptake, and correlate with retesting rates and early treatment initiation.

future_directions.title: Pilot CF NBS using a cost-effective, context-appropriate approach in high-burden regions
future_directions.rationale: CF data in India are limited and standard protocols are lacking. Implement a pilot combining first-tier IRT with a targeted mutation panel (regional CFTR variants) or reflex DNA testing where feasible. Evaluate false-positive/false-negative rates, cost per detected case, and feasibility within existing laboratory workflows. Use results to inform broader policy decisions on CF screening inclusion.

future_directions.title: Establish a national NBS policy framework and funding model for expansion
future_directions.rationale: India currently lacks a nationwide NBS program integrated into health policy. Convene stakeholders to define a minimum panel, standardized protocols, data reporting, and quality assurance. Develop a scalable funding plan, including public–private partnerships, to support equipment, training, confirmatory testing, and follow-up services across diverse settings.

future_directions.title: Create a national multicenter prevalence study of major treatable IEMs with standardized protocols
future_directions.rationale: There is a paucity of population-based prevalence data for many IEMs in India. Design a multicenter, representative study across regions with harmonized case definitions, sampling, and confirmatory testing. This will inform resource allocation, public health prioritization, and regional screening emphasis.

future_directions.title: Strengthen laboratory capacity, QA, and cross-platform standardization across centers
future_directions.rationale: The current study used DELFIA/Revvity platforms; to enable scale, establish external quality assurance programs, inter-lab proficiency testing, and cross-validation of alternative platforms. Develop centralized training, standard operating procedures, and data-sharing practices to ensure consistent performance and reliable results across sites.

future_directions.title: Integrate digital health and telemedicine to support diagnosis, counseling, and long-term management
future_directions.rationale: Digital solutions can bridge geographic barriers and improve adherence to follow-up and treatment. Develop a secure platform for remote counseling, result interpretation, appointment scheduling, and treatment monitoring. Pilot in both urban and rural settings, evaluating user engagement, time-to-treatment, and health outcomes.
